actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The README describes an Isaac Sim workflow: install the NVIDIA driver, Omniverse and Isaac Sim, open the USD asset from the content browser, and press play to start the simulation.
The piper_description CMakeLists is an ament_cmake description build: it installs the launch, meshes, rviz, urdf and mujoco_model directories and defines no executable target.
The piper_description manifest declares ament_cmake with runtime dependencies joint_state_publisher, joint_state_publisher_gui, rviz2 and xacro; it declares no message, service or action definition.
The display launch starts robot_state_publisher, joint_state_publisher (or its GUI) and rviz2, and starts no controller or command node.
The xacro adds a gazebo_ros2_control plugin that loads its controller parameters from piper_gazebo/config/ros2_controllers.yaml; the piper_gazebo package and that file are not part of this clone.
The MJCF root declares the model name piper_description and the compiler angle in radians.
The MJCF worldbody is a fixed-base chain of six hinge joints (joint1 to joint6) followed by two slide joints (joint7 and joint8); it declares no free joint.

The hinge joint ranges are joint1 -2.618 to 2.168 rad, joint2 0 to 3.14 rad, joint3 -2.967 to 0 rad, joint4 -1.745 to 1.745 rad, joint5 -1.22 to 1.22 rad and joint6 -2.0944 to 2.0944 rad; the slide joint ranges are joint7 0 to 0.035 and joint8 -0.035 to 0.
The actuator section declares eight position actuators, joint1 to joint8, and every actuator sets ctrllimited=true with an explicit ctrlrange; it also sets forcelimited=true and a forcerange.
The MJCF asset section names ten mesh files under ../meshes: base_link, link1 to link8 and gripper_base.
The MJCF contains no <option> element and no timestep attribute.

The actuator ctrlranges are wider than the joint ranges for joint1 (ctrlrange -2.618 to 2.618, range -2.618 to 2.168), joint4 (-1.832 to 1.832 against -1.745 to 1.745), joint6 (-3.14158 to 3.14158 against -2.0944 to 2.0944), joint7 (0 to 0.0475 against 0 to 0.035) and joint8 (-0.0475 to 0 against -0.035 to 0); joint2's ctrlrange ends at 3.14158 and its range at 3.14.
The card's second model, piper_no_gripper_description.xml, is a six-joint MJCF with six position actuators and no gripper; it is not the model this package serves.
The piper_description manifest declares its licence as 'TODO: License declaration'.
The vendored realsense2_description manifest declares the Apache License 2.0.

determinism.notes: The stand-in moves each actuated joint by a fixed fraction toward its control value from the zero reset state; it has no seed input and its motion is not MuJoCo's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the pinned MJCF for the joint dimensions and the per-actuator ctrlranges but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control value, so trajectories, contacts, actuator dynamics and the model's inertials are not MuJoCo's

the model's eight <position> actuators are position servos with kp and forcerange; the fake's first-order step is not a position servo and ignores kp, forcerange, damping, inertia and the joint ranges, so it follows targets beyond the joint ranges that the wider ctrlranges admit
the MJCF declares no <option timestep>, so the fake uses MuJoCo's library default 0.002 s as a placeholder; the reported 2.0 ms comes from the fake, not from a line of the clone
the fake has no mj_getState/mj_setState/mj_stateSize, so the bridge uses its basic checkpoint profile: time, qpos, qvel and ctrl are restored, not MuJoCo's full integration state
no mesh, texture, collision, contact, equality, tendon or sensor is loaded or resolved by the stand-in; the bridge exposes qpos, qvel, ctrl and time, not camera, inertial or sensor arrays
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so the stand-in was not compared with the real engine and no Isaac Sim or USD asset was opened
the package serves the card's models[0] only, a description and asset repository's MJCF, and no physical PiPER robot is modelled or driven

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulated world stops advancing: after an e-stop the server refuses step and reset until an operator reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
